translation_en: Abu al-Rabi‘ Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, and Ahmad explained some of it to me. Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning what the people of the slander said about her, and how Allah declared her innocent of it. Al-Zuhri said: Each of them told me part of her account. Some had retained more of it than others and had remembered it more firmly. I have retained from each of them the report he narrated to me from ‘Aishah, and some parts of their reports confirm others. They said that ‘Aishah said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended to travel, he drew lots among his wives. Whichever one's lot came out, he would take her with him. On one expedition he undertook, he drew lots among us, and my lot came out. I went with him after the verse about the veil had been revealed. I was carried in a howdah and put down in it. We travelled until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished that expedition and was returning. When we had drawn near to Madinah, he announced one night that we would set off. I got up when they announced the departure and walked past the army. When I had finished what I needed to do, I came back to the riding place and felt my chest. My necklace, made of beads from the shells of Zafar, had broken. I went back to look for it, and searching for it delayed me. The men who used to prepare my mount came and lifted my howdah, placed it on the camel I rode, and set it off, thinking that I was inside it. At that time women were light in weight; they had not grown heavy or been covered with flesh. They ate only a little food. So when the men lifted the howdah and carried it away, they did not notice any unusual weight. I was a young girl. They sent the camel on and continued. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their stopping place, but no one was there. I went to the place where I had been staying and thought that they would notice I was missing and come back for me. While I was sitting there, sleep overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. In the morning he reached the place where I was and saw the dark outline of a sleeping person. He came to me. He had seen me before the veil was prescribed. I woke when he said, ‘We belong to Allah, and to Him we return,’ as he made his camel kneel. He put its foreleg down, and I mounted it. He then led the camel with me until we reached the army after they had stopped to rest in the heat of midday. Some people were ruined, and the one who took the leading part in the slander was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We arrived in Madinah, where I became ill for a month. During that time the people were repeating what the slanderers had said. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not see from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only come in, greet me, and say, ‘How is that one?’ I did not know anything about the matter until I had recovered. Then I went out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi‘, the place where we relieved ourselves. We used to go out only from one night to the next. This was before we had built nearby latrines, and our practice was like that of the early Arabs in the open country or when travelling. Umm Mistah bint Abi Ruhm and I were walking when she stumbled over her cloak and said, ‘May Mistah be ruined!’ I said to her, ‘What a bad thing to say! Are you insulting a man who was present at Badr?’ She said, ‘You poor woman, have you not heard what they are saying?’ Then she told me what the slanderers were saying. My illness grew worse because of it. When I returned home, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted me, and said, ‘How is that one?’ I said, ‘Will you let me go to my parents?’ I wanted to make sure of the report from them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission, and I went to my parents. I said to my mother, ‘What are people talking about?’ She said, ‘My daughter, take it lightly. By Allah, it is rare for a beautiful woman who is loved by a man and has co-wives not to have them speak against her.’ I said, ‘Glory be to Allah! Are people really talking about this?’ I spent that night until morning with tears that would not stop and without sleeping. In the morning, when the revelation had been delayed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd to consult them about separating from his wife. Usamah advised him according to the affection he knew the Prophet had for his family. Usamah said, ‘They are your family, Messenger of Allah, and by Allah, we know nothing about them except good.’ ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah has not placed any restriction on you; there are many women besides her. Ask the servant girl and she will tell you the truth.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for Barirah and said, ‘Barirah, have you seen anything about her that makes you doubt her?’ Barirah said, ‘No, by the One who sent you with the truth. I have seen nothing in her that I could criticize, except that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while the dough is rising, and then the household animal comes and eats it.’ That day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood up and sought support against ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said, ‘Who will help me against a man whose harm to my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good. They have also mentioned a man about whom I know nothing except good, and he never entered my family’s home except when he was with me.’ Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will help you against him. If he is from the Aws, we will strike his neck, and if he is one of our brothers from the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command against him.’ Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj, then stood up. He had previously been a righteous man, but anger overcame him. He said, ‘By the life of Allah, you have lied. You will not kill him, and you are not able to do that.’ Usayd ibn Hudayr stood up and said, ‘By the life of Allah, you have lied. By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.’ The two clans, Aws and Khazraj, became stirred up until they were about to fight, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. He came down and calmed them until they fell silent, and then he was silent. I cried that whole day, with tears that would not stop, and without sleeping. The next morning my parents were with me. I had cried for two nights and a day, until I thought that the crying would split my liver. While they were sitting with me and I was crying, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to come in. I let her in, and she sat and cried with me. While we were like that, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in and sat down. He had not sat with me since the day people had said what they said about me. A month had passed without any revelation being sent to him concerning me. He began by bearing witness, then said, ‘Aishah, I have heard such-and-such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare you innocent. If you have committed a sin, then ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant admits a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance.’ When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished speaking, my tears dried up until I could no longer feel a single drop. I said to my father, ‘Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.’ He said, ‘By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I said to my mother, ‘Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf about what he said.’ She said, ‘By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I was a young girl and did not recite much of the Quran. I said, ‘By Allah, I know that you have heard what people are saying, and it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent—and Allah knows that I am innocent—you will not believe me. But if I admit something to you, while Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I can find no example for you and me except the father of Yusuf, who said, “So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe” (12:18).’ Then I turned over on my bed, hoping that Allah would declare me innocent. But by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning me. I considered myself too insignificant for Quran to be revealed about my matter. I had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in which Allah declared me innocent. By Allah, he had not left his seat, and no one from the household had gone out, when revelation came down to him. He was overcome by the state that used to come over him, until sweat like pearls ran down from him on a cold day. When that state passed from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling. The first words he said to me were, ‘Aishah, praise Allah, for Allah has declared you innocent.’ My mother said to me, ‘Get up and go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I said, ‘No, by Allah, I will not get up to go to him, and I will praise none but Allah.’ Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you’ and the verses that follow (24:11). When Allah revealed this declaring me innocent, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to support Mistah ibn Uthathah because of their kinship, said, ‘By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah again after what he said about Aishah.’ Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘Those of you who possess grace and abundance should not swear…’ up to His words, ‘…All-Forgiving, Most Merciful’ (24:22). Abu Bakr said, ‘Indeed, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me.’ So he returned to supporting Mistah as he had done before. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, also asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about me. He said, ‘Zaynab, what have you known or seen?’ She replied, ‘Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing about her except good.’ ‘Aishah said: She was the one who used to compete with me for the Prophet’s favor, but Allah protected her through her piety. He said: Fulayh narrated to us from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah and ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, the same report. He said: Fulayh narrated to us from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman and Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, the same report.
